findings.rationale: Project replay reports a violation only when both the declaration and event contain a field and their values differ. An event that omits a declared model, prompt, retriever, or output_schema therefore passes, and declared tools are collected but never checked at all. Such incomplete logs can be reported replay_conformant despite not satisfying the component contract.

Projects support multiple ai_component blocks, but replay reduces the whole project to one mutable summary. Each new header overwrites only the component name without clearing prior fields, so the final component can inherit another component's contract; --component can select only that final name and rejects every earlier valid component.

Header discovery and brace-depth tracking do not recognize line comments. Text such as `// dataset old {}` is parsed as a real block, while an unmatched brace in a comment changes nesting or produces an unterminated-block error. Valid commented-out declarations can therefore alter or invalidate the parsed project.

find_comparator iterates every byte offset but slices the UTF-8 string as s[i..]. Any non-ASCII character before a comparator causes an invalid character-boundary panic instead of producing a parse or inconclusive result, allowing ordinary source input to crash the CLI.

The parser stores observed_property.window, but run_ai_drift passes only the optional CLI window to the evaluator. Without --window the declared window is discarded rather than used as the default, so the executed drift evaluation does not honor the selected property's configuration.

Compatibility output normalizes every component name independently and concatenates the resulting artifact blocks without checking uniqueness. Distinct valid names such as FooBar and foo_bar both become foo_bar, yielding duplicate artifact declarations and an ambiguous or invalid dbsystem fragment.
